newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Coffee surges ahead, wheat and oil decline.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Coffee surges ahead, wheat and oil decline.

text.p: World coffee prices surged ahead on Tuesday, boosted by news of a lower Colombian output estimate and a strike at Brazil's key port of Santos.
The New York market saw speculative buying amid a positive technical and fundamental outlook, traders said.
Elsewhere world commodity markets looked mixed as wheat and oil prices took a hit, but copper led a push higher in industrial metals. Gold also slipped lower.

The chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, Jorge Cardenas, said after Monday's close that the country's output totalled 10 million 60-kg bags in 1996/1997 (April-March), down from about 14 million in the same period a year ago.
Production between April and September was seen at about 4.5 million bags, he said.

Meanwhile in Brazil, the world's number one producer, stevedores at the port of Santos began a strike on Tuesday for an indefinite period, bringing loading and unloading to a halt, a union official said.
The official said the strike could spread to a national level on Wednesday.
Robusta coffee futures for May were trading around $25 higher at $1,578.00 per tonne in London's Tuesday afternoon.
Profit-taking and milder weather took the steam out of a recent take-off in grain prices, with wheat falling back around three cents per bushel to $4.20 in Chicago futures pits.

U.S. wheat futures posted small gains early on Tuesday in electronic trading and similar gains followed at the open of formal trade in Chicago, but prices soon slipped as profit-taking with aggressive fund selling was noted after Monday's rally.
A report late on Monday forecasting rain in May also eased drought worries for wheat crops in Europe.

Chicago July soft red winter wheat had been boosted on Monday by concerns that a hard freeze over the weekend had caused widespread damage to U.S. crops, but Tuesday's news that temperatures overnight did not fall enough to cause more damage dragged wheat prices down.
A turnaround in the metals, first seen on Monday, continued and brokerage Rudolf Wolff said in a report that it was "perhaps an indication that the funds are losing their appetite for the downside".
Copper and aluminium both moved higher on the London Metal Exchange.
Crude oil prices for benchmark North Sea Brent Blend held lower, subdued by reports of selling and sentiment that tension between Iran and the West, which boosted prices on Monday, was easing.
The May Brent futures contract, which expires at the end of Tuesday's session, was trading around $18 a barrel in London's Tuesday afternoon.
Gold headed lower after a New York sell-off on lower-than-expected U.S. consumer inflation data, which showed a rise of 0.1 percent compared to forecasts of 0.2 percent.
Tuesday also saw cocoa climb, while sugar drifted lower.
